limits: No production source or project dependencies changed.
Two style properties only; no final 77-property implementation or production generator/template-compiler pipeline.
React 19.3.0, React DOM 19.3.0, @lit/react 1.0.8 and scheduler 0.28.0 loaded from integrity-checked archives in memory; no installation into the project.
Playwright 1.63.0 and Firefox/WebKit test binaries were placed in a dedicated temporary test cache, without changing the existing global browser cache.
CEM property/attribute links and inheritance were exercised with analyzer 0.11.0 and its bundled TypeScript 5.4.2; real project paths/exports and complete source metadata remain unverified.
Browser cases are bounded feasibility checks, not approval of the full shared module or migration.
Expected failing comparison controls are preserved. Undefined values may be omitted or serialized as null in JSON; source checks and additional strict absence booleans establish the absence case.

decisions.decision: Omitted CSS styling inputs read undefined. Visual defaults are supplied through CSS. Explicitly supplied values remain readable as those inputs. Semantic state properties such as open/checked retain their separate default contracts.
decisions.basis: Peter's explicit blocking-tool answer after Material Web/Chakra/Radix/Pro source comparison
decisions.limits: Does not approve complete styling engine or full inventory row.

communicationClarification.rule: A wait-what repair and every decision question must contain all decision-relevant context inside the dialog. Use plain language and visible organization. Do not shorten away details; commentary outside the dialog is not sufficient.

defaultReadResearch.status: Captured; recommendation selected by Peter as C-STYLE-02
defaultReadResearch.finding: CSS distinguishes declarations supplied by an author from resolved appearance. Lit permits defaults. Chakra supplies a Stack default internally but has no comparable DOM getter. No universal rule requires absent custom properties to return undefined.
defaultReadResearch.recommendation: Absent CSS styling inputs read undefined; visual defaults apply through CSS. Peter subsequently selected this as C-STYLE-02. Constructor override failures do not disprove a correctly implemented resolved-default getter.

questionFormattingResearch.finding: The installed request renderer passes question string to a plain div via s1; no Markdown parser or whitespace-preserving class. Options render label and description separately. No rich text/layout field in callable schema.

experiment.conclusion: In Chrome 153, normal newlines, U+2028 and U+2029 did not create paragraph breaks under the renderer's normal whitespace layout. Markdown and HTML remained literal text. These are isolated rendering tests, not a live-question end-to-end check.

questionFormattingResearch.rule: Use supported native blocks: shared decision context in question and option-specific evidence/consequences in distinct label/description blocks. Do not send pseudo-headings/newline lists expecting preserved layout. Rich paragraphs require a renderer change; no such change made or authorized. Keep full decision-relevant meaning inside dialog.

webFollowup.finding: Expanded targeted searches found no documented rich-formatting argument or verified workaround for the installed desktop question renderer. Current upstream tool schema exposes only id/header/question/options(label,description); no HTML, Markdown, preview or layout argument. App-server supports distinct MCP elicitation, but no callable general elicitation question tool was found in this session. The structured-form discussion is a user proposal, not implemented support.
webFollowup.qualification: Do not claim there is absolutely no way. Formatting through this available tool/installed renderer is unsupported; changing renderer or building another question surface are different engineering tasks, not proven ready alternatives.

questionFormattingResearch.userDisposition: Peter declined building a replacement tool and explicitly requested continuing with the existing question tool. Keep using the blocking Plan-mode path for decisions; no agent countdown. New tool research is not a build task.

defaultReadLibraryComparison.status: Source review; no new browser tests for this reference comparison. Peter subsequently selected preserve absence as C-STYLE-02.

material.finding: Button's public JS interface declares softDisabled=false, trailingIcon=false, href=''. Spacing is CSS: :host gap:8px, logical padding from internal CSS custom properties, inner .button gap:inherit. No gap JS property in inspected Button API. This supports separating visual CSS defaults from semantic JS defaults, but is not an equivalent absent-style-property getter contract.

chakra.finding: Destructures omitted gap to '0.5rem' inside Stack. props.gap remains absent; the ref is HTMLDivElement, not a public Stack instance. It does not establish how a Lit style getter should read.

radix.finding: gap defs have no default. extractProps applies defaults only when configured, skips absent style values, translates supplied props to classes/styles and removes consumed styling props. Ref is native DOM; no matching Flex.gap getter.

pro.finding: Full file read: HStacks with omitted gap alongside explicit gap='2'. Shows authoring with default and override; no DOM getter contract.

defaultReadLibraryComparison.conclusion: No exact common getter contract among the compared libraries. Recommend undefined for absent house CSS styling inputs as an explicit house choice, CSS supplies visible default, semantic properties keep own defaults. Do not label recommendation as Material's precise implementation or universal best practice.

nextStep: Complete shared styling contract: actual package CEM path/export normalization and compiler integration, declaration-order rules for every supported input path, exact types/token and density mappings, responsive validation/condition mapping and target syntax; then finish layout/typography rows. Bounded probes do not satisfy full Phase 5 style pipeline gate.

reproduction.instructions: The embedded runner/test strings retain the in-memory fixtures and integrity-checked archive acquisition. Browser driver scripts use the dedicated temporary cache recorded under otherEngines.driver; that cache is not a portable committed dependency and may need re-creation. Temporary server ports in recorded outputs are historical. No production source was installed or changed.
reproduction.browserScope: Chrome 153, Firefox 155 and WebKit 26.6; WebKit automation is not an actual Safari application test.
